sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: MongoDB interview questions cover the document data model in interview depth — schema design (embedded vs referenced), indexes (compound, multikey, text, geo), the aggregation pipeline, sharding and zone sharding, replica sets and read concerns, consistency trade-offs (eventual, causal, linearizable reads), and integration with Spring Data MongoDB. Expect senior interviews to compare MongoDB to a relational store and probe on operational concerns (rebalancing, backup, election).

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
MongoDB is a **document store** with a strong query language.

- Schema = **embedded vs referenced** — embed for read locality, reference for write boundaries.
- **Aggregation pipeline** = SQL's GROUP BY + window + projection, all in one.
- **Indexes** — single, compound, multikey (arrays), text, geo.
- **Replica set** — primary + secondaries; **sharding** for horizontal scale.
- **Read concerns** — local / majority / linearizable; pick by consistency need.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **The 16 MB document limit** — rare in practice but interviewers love it.
- **Compound index ordering** matters — leftmost prefix wins.
- **No joins** — denormalise, or use `$lookup` knowing it's the perf cost.
- **Multi-document transactions** — supported in 4+ replica sets, but design for atomic per-document.
- **Sharding key** is permanent — picking it badly costs a re-sharding.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd model the entity as <embedded | referenced> because <access pattern>, index it on <compound key honouring leftmost prefix>, run reads against secondaries with read concern <level>, and shard on <key> if writes outgrow a single replica set."*
